limitations: Unique IPs are not physical controllers; one address may represent multiple controllers.
Tagged service records were excluded from endpoint selection; IPs with both tagged and untagged records can remain, as can unidentified decoys.
One landing-page request per eligible IP cannot establish whether the device is vulnerable or compromised.
No credentials, controller changes, redirects, retries, port scans, or JS execution are used.
A timeout or TLS error is not evidence that equipment is offline.
Only aggregates are retained; no raw IP addresses or page contents are persisted.
Index partitions were collected sequentially and differed by one IP/service; the inventory is not an atomic fleet snapshot.
The 3-second socket timeout and normal TLS certificate verification make this a conservative reachability check; redirects and alternate endpoints were not tried.
A visible web UI version is not controller firmware. Last-Modified matches are build inferences, and shared timestamps remain ambiguous.

retrospectiveAudit.bodyReadUndercountRisk: The original reader waited for up to 16 KiB or end-of-body. A locally reproduced server sent HTTP 200 and a valid StoreView title but was classified as timeout because it kept the body open. Failure stages and HTTP-status aggregates were not retained, so the number of affected timeouts cannot be reconstructed.
retrospectiveAudit.honeypotIntersectionReason: Only aggregate outcomes were retained; no IP-to-outcome linkage or overlap counter survives. Excluding tagged service records did not exclude IPs with other tagged service records.
retrospectiveAudit.scope: No new controller requests were made for this audit. The checker was corrected and tested locally; the original measurement has not been rerun.
